title: Family Apartments & Kids' Activities in Slano 2027
metaDescription: Where to stay with kids in Slano, Croatia: apartments near pebble beaches, prices in euros, day trips to Ston, Trsteno and Mljet, plus practical tips.
content: ## Why Slano Works for Families Slano is a small town on a bay about 2 km wide, 30 km northwest of Dubrovnik, roughly 35-40 minutes by car on the Adriatic Highway. The bay is sheltered, the water is calm, and the harbour promenade is flat and easy for strollers. Nightlife is minimal, which is the main reason families choose it over Dubrovnik or Cavtat. The beaches are pebble, not sand. Water shoes are a necessity for toddlers and young children, and beach mats make the stones comfortable. Most apartments do not supply them, so buy them in town or bring them. ## Best Family Apartments in Slano ### What to look for Three things matter more than a sea view: a kitchen with a dishwasher or washing machine, air conditioning in the bedrooms, and free private parking. Slano has steep streets, and a ground-floor or middle-floor unit saves a lot of effort with strollers and beach bags. ### Apartments close to the water - **Apartments Riva / Vila Riva** sit about 50 m from the pebble beach in the town centre. Units have a kitchenette with a dishwasher, air conditioning and a seating area. The property has a pool, which suits younger children. - **Luxury Villa Salt** is a well-rated apartment house, with an average rate near €60 per night and a 9.6/10 guest score. Families describe the apartments as spacious, with a well-equipped kitchen. - **Slano Bay Apartments** offer 40-60 m² units with air conditioning and sea views. Apartment 3 has two bedrooms and sleeps up to four. - **Apartments Nine Slano** are about 2 minutes on foot from the beaches and 5 minutes from restaurants. They have a shared shaded patio, free parking, and a separate children's room in some units. ### Larger groups **Apartment Bobić** has three bedrooms and two bathrooms, sleeps six, and costs around €135 per night. It is inland, 600 m from the seaside, so a car is helpful. Holiday homes with private pools in nearby villages such as Sladenovići sleep up to eight, but need a car for every trip. ## Beaches for Children - **San Jeronimo Beach** is in town, about 70 m from central apartments. - **Koceljevići Beach** is roughly 300-700 m from the centre, depending on where you stay. - **Grgurići Beach** is about 1.1 km away, and **Banja Beach** about 1.3 km. The central beach is the easiest for short days with toddlers. For quieter swimming, a 10-15 minute walk past the marina leads to less crowded stretches. They have no sunbeds, so bring your own mats and umbrella. The bay has many small fish, so a mask and snorkel is the cheapest entertainment for school-age children. ## Things to Do with Kids Near Slano ### In town Kids can swim, rent a kayak or SUP board in summer, fish from the harbour and eat ice cream along the waterfront. Several apartments include SUP boards or beach chairs, so ask before booking. ### Trsteno Arboretum (about 13 km) The arboretum is a 15-minute drive toward Dubrovnik. Its shaded paths, fountains and old plane trees give children a break from the heat. Tickets cost roughly €10-15 for adults in season, and children's rates are lower. Check current prices before going. ### Ston and Mali Ston (about 18 km) The Walls of Ston are about 5.5 km long, one of the longest fortification systems in Europe. Children can walk the short section to the first tower, but the stone steps are steep and slippery. Start early and bring water, because there is no shade. Mali Ston is known for oysters, and it also has simple grilled fish that children usually eat. ### Mljet National Park (day trip) Ferries to Mljet leave from Prapratno on the Pelješac peninsula, about 25 km from Slano, and take roughly 45 minutes. At the park, children can swim in the Veliko Jezero and Malo Jezero saltwater lakes and rent bikes for the lake path. Book vehicle ferry spots ahead in July and August. ### Dubrovnik (30 km) The old town is crowded and hot in midday. Go early or in the late afternoon. The city walls are not suitable for strollers, and the entry fee is high for a family of four. This sounds like a must-do, but with children under six it is usually better to skip the walls and spend the money on a boat trip. ## Local Tips for Parents - **Rent a car.** Public buses on the coast run, but not often enough for family day trips. - **Shop in the morning.** Small supermarkets in Slano close earlier than those in Dubrovnik, and fruit stands appear along the road in summer. - **Book early for July and August.** Apartments with pools and sea views fill by spring. - **Shoulder season is best.** In late May, June and September the sea is warm, prices drop, and the town is calmer. - **Ask about cots and high chairs.** Several apartment houses supply them on request at no cost. ## Getting to Slano Dubrovnik Airport is about 50 km away, roughly a 50-minute drive. Transfer by taxi usually costs €60-90, and car rental gives the most flexibility. Parking in Slano is free at most apartments.

faq.question: Is Slano good for families with young children?
faq.answer: Yes. The bay is sheltered, the water is calm, and the town is quiet and walkable. The beaches are pebble, so children need water shoes.

faq.question: How much does a family apartment in Slano cost?
faq.answer: In summer, expect about €60-140 per night for a family apartment. Larger three-bedroom units near €135 per night are common. Prices are lower in May, June and September.

faq.question: How far is Slano from Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Slano is 30 km northwest of Dubrovnik. The drive takes about 35-40 minutes by car. Dubrovnik Airport is roughly 50 km away.

faq.question: Does Slano have sandy beaches?
faq.answer: No. The beaches in Slano, including San Jeronimo, Koceljevići, Grgurići and Banja, are pebble. Bring water shoes and beach mats.

faq.question: What are the best day trips from Slano with kids?
faq.answer: Trsteno Arboretum (about 13 km) is the easiest. Ston and its walls are about 18 km away, and Mljet National Park is reached by ferry from Prapratno. Dubrovnik works best early or late in the day.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Slano?
faq.answer: A car is strongly recommended. Buses are infrequent, and the main family attractions are spread along the coast. Most apartments offer free parking.

quickAnswer: Slano suits families who want a quiet bay instead of Dubrovnik crowds. Apartments within 50-150 m of the pebble beaches cost roughly €60-140 per night in summer. Calm, shallow water, kitchens, free parking and day trips to Ston, Trsteno and Mljet keep children busy. Dubrovnik is 30 km away.
